name: erdem-antigravity-adapter
description: Antigravity adapter for the Erdem Design System: one skill (erdem) and an optional small project AGENTS.md block. It consumes the canonical protocol and the project-intel engine; it contains neither.

supportedEnvironment.operatingSystems: no platform-specific code; developed and tested on Windows 11 only (macOS and Linux untested)
supportedEnvironment.antigravity: IDE 1.107.0 verified for documentation only; see verifiedWith

verifiedWith.evidence: bundled customization guide (builtin/skills/agy-customizations) and string checks in the installed application files; no agent session was run
verifiedWith.runtimeVerification: NOT VERIFIABLE from outside the application: see README, Runtime verification

verifiedCapabilities: adapter files install, update, uninstall and are diagnosed correctly in temporary fixture directories (automated tests)
the launcher, context, handoff-check and intel commands run under Node outside Antigravity (automated tests)
the documented customization locations exist in the installed product documentation: <project>/.agents/skills, ~/.gemini/config/, AGENTS.md and GEMINI.md directory rules
unverifiedCapabilities: that the Antigravity agent discovers and activates the installed skill (not observable without running an agent session)
that the agent runs the launcher command (command execution depends on the user's permission policy)
that AGENTS.md content is loaded for a given workspace and when
user-scope skill discovery from ~/.gemini/config/skills (documented as a global customization root; skills layout documented for customization roots in general)
behavior in Antigravity 2.0 and the agy command line (agy is not installed in the development environment)
capabilities: skill: erdem (design, implementation and mixed tasks, review, context, handoff)
agents-md-block: small managed block in the project AGENTS.md (project scope, opt-in)
context command: engine status mapped to missing, current, stale, unverifiable, partial, unavailable
handoff drift check: compares a handoff's changed files with the working tree
safe-install: dry run, idempotent, ownership markers, shared-folder detection, no hooks/MCP/rules changes
notUsed: hooks.json (documented: PreInvocation can inject context, but hooks run through the host shell, fire on every model call, and could not be run here; a shared hooks.json would also need merging with the user's own hooks)
mcp_config.json (can hold credentials; never read or written)
plugins, rules/*.md with triggers, workflows (not needed; the skill and AGENTS.md block cover the boundary)
compatibilityNotes: Locations and formats come from the customization guide bundled with Antigravity IDE 1.107.0 (workspace root .agents/, global root ~/.gemini/config/, skills/<name>/SKILL.md with name and description front matter, AGENTS.md and GEMINI.md directory rules without front matter, hooks.json, progressive disclosure: only skill names and descriptions are injected).

The project skill folder .agents/skills/erdem is also read by Codex. If the Codex adapter owns it, this adapter keeps it and installs nothing there; if this adapter owns it first, the Codex installer reports a conflict and does not overwrite it.
Antigravity changes quickly; re-run the doctor and consult the live documentation (antigravity.google/docs) after upgrades.
If the agent cannot run commands, the protocol still works through direct inspection (adapters/GENERIC.md section 9).
